description.narrative: The Road Network Upgrading Sector Project will upgrade priority sections of the national road network. The project will finance the upgrading of the trans-island road from Manatuto to Natarbora, which will greatly improve national connectivity and directly support the government's petroleum and gas developments on the south coast. The project will also finance the preparation of other high-priority road links. The proposed project will (i) upgrade and climate-proof about 117 kilometers (km) of principal national roads, (ii) expand the road maintenance program of the Ministry of Public Works (MPW), and (iii) prepare detailed designs and environmental and social due diligence for upgrading 169 km of principal national roads through future projects.

description.narrative: Ministy of Public Works (MPW) provides a more reliable and safer road network

30% reduction in travel time from Manatuto to Natarbora (15% reduction in travel time in other subproject roads) Achievement: 2.45 Progress/Status: Civil works for Manatuto-Laclubar Junction - Natarbora road sections under Loans 3020/3021, and Grant 0404 have been completed.
Civil works for Baucau to Lautem, and Maubara-Karimbala + Atabae Mota Ain have also been completed. Data Source: Project completion report prepared by MPW

Rate of road accident on project roads does not increase Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Civil works for Manatuto-Laclubar Junction - Natarbora road sections under Loans 3020/3021, and Grant 0404 have been completed.
Civil works for Baucau to Lautem, and Maubara-Karimbala + Atabae Mota Ain have also been completed.
No road accidents reported along Baucau-Lautem; Maubara-Karimbala-Atabae-Mota Ain road sections based on construction supervision consultant's report in October 2022. Data Source: National accident statistics produced by the Timor-Leste National Police Force (PNTL) Base year: 2013 Baseline value: Y
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Expand performance-based road maintenance Indicator: By December 2021, at least 650 km of national roads (45%) receive routine maintenance under a performance-based contract in accordance with DRBFC's annual plan Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Performance-based maintenance (PBM) period for Manatuto-Laclubar Junction (35.13km) started on 15 September 2020 and completed on 15 September 2022. PBM for Laclubar Junction-Natarbora started on 8 November 2021 and completed on 8 November 2023.
In 2020, TIM Government has requested extension of Loan 3020/3021 completion until 30 June 2022 to accommodate DNP and PBM for Laclubar Junction to Natarbora section (i.e., DNP from December 2019 to November 2020; and PBM from December 2020 to November 2021).
Another extension of Loan 3020/3021 closing date from 30 June 2022 to 31 December 2023 was approved by ADB in June 2022 due to Government's request in May 2022 to accommodate the 2-year PBM period; settle pending payments to the contractors and CSC.; and settle pending safeguards issues.
L3020 3021: All WAs for liquidation were submitted for processing to financially close the loans by Q1 2026. Data Source: Annual road condition surverys by DRBFC
DRBFC road maintenance program annual reports DRBFC road maintenance program annual reports

Output: Generate awareness of road safety and transport-related social issues Indicator: 100% of construction workers and at least 80% of roadside inhabitants recieve education in gender and transport security, and HIV/AIDS awareness by end of 2017 Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: On HIV awareness seminar involving the workers, their families and the communities, four (4) sessions were already conducted by the Contractor of Package 1 (Manatuto-Laclubar Junction) between April 2016 and November 2018 involving a total of 309 participants, while another two (2) were conducted by the Contractor of Package 2 (Laclubar Junction-Natarbora between September 2017 and March 2018 involving 44 participants, as of Q1 2018. Disaggregated data will be requested from PMU.
For L3341/3342: -100% of Baucau-Lautem, and Maubara-Karimbala-Mota Ain road section workers have received HIV/AIDS awareness education based on October 2020 report. -Figures for roadside inhabitants to be requested from PMU.
Data Source: Records of training of construction workers and roadside communities maintained by the Ministry of Health

Output: Generate awareness of road safety and transport-related social issues Indicator: At least 80% of children and 80% of women in roadside communities receive road safety awareness education by the end of 2021 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: An earlier discussion with National Police of Timor-Leste was initially held sometime in March 2018 to coordinate the conduct of road safety awareness program and campaign in one completed loan funded project of the government, with the aim of replicating the approach with the other projects nearing completion particularly RNUSP. However, because of changes in government, as a result of the last election, the road safety awareness campaign was not finalized. Data Source: Records of road safety education delivered to schools maintained by the Ministry of Education

Exact number of local workers hired and % of women have yet to be determined/assessed. Data Source: Project monitoring reports from MPW

Output: Upgrade and climate proof national roads Indicator: 1a. By the end of 2021, the average road roughness on about 178 km of national roads (the project roads) falls from an average of 8 m/km to 4 m/km. Achievement: 4 Progress/Status: Civil works for 35.13km Manatuto-Laclubar Junction and 44.6km Laclubar Junction-Natarbora under Loans 3020/3021, and Grant 0404 have been completed in 2018 and 2019, respectively.
Under Loans 3341/3342, civil works for 58.94km Baucau-Lautem, and 37.8km Maubara-Karimbala + Atabae Mota Ain have been completed. Data Source: Annual road condition surveys by DRBFC; project monitoring reports from MPW

Output: Generate awareness of road safety and transport-related social issues Indicator: Rate of increase of fatal injury due to road crash is less than the rate of growth in the vehicle fleet Achievement: N Progress/Status: MPW has not reported any road crash in the project's road sections. Rate will be assessed. Data Source: Records of crash fatalities maintained by PNTL and MOH Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Generate awareness of road safety and transport-related social issues Indicator: Road safety council is established by December 2021 Achievement: N Progress/Status: The project intended to support the creation of a National Road Safety Council and the formulation of National Road Safety Action Plan. The focal point was envisaged to be the National Directorate of Road Security under the Ministry of Interior , together with the National Police of Timor-Leste. For initial support, a Road Safety Specialist was recruited by PMU to assist in the development of policies and strategies for road safety through the conduct of workshop with key stakeholders to identify capacity, willingness and roles of key stakeholders. For the part of the Ministry, an earlier discussion with PNTL was initially held sometime in March 2018 to coordinate the conduct of road safety awareness program and campaign in one completed loan funded project of the government, with the aim of replicating the approach with the other projects nearing completion particularly RNUSP. However, because of changes in government, as a result of the last election, the road safety awareness campaign was not finalized. Data Source: Official memoranda of the MPW Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Prepare detailed designs for future priority road links Indicator: Detailed engineering design for damaged sections of Manatuto-Natarbora road section by Q4 2025 Progress/Status: Additional scope based on approved memo dated 30 June 2022.
Per MPW during the review mission in November 2022, it now intends to use uncommitted G0404-TIM funds for DED preparation for damaged areas of Manatuto-Natarbora road section. ADB mission team informed MPW to provide ADB with a formal advice/letter on cancellation of original request along with its proposed revised utilization plan for G0404-TIM uncommitted proceeds.
ADB on 27 December 2023 provided no objection to the government's request for minor change in scope and the extension of grant closing date, including (i) cancellation of Lamara Bridge FS Update and DED Preparation; (ii) utilization of grant proceeds for DED Preparation for damaged sections of Manatuto-Natarbora road section; and (iii) extension of Grant Closing Date by 24 months from 31 December 2023 to 31 December 2025. Through its letter dated 20 November 2025, MPW requested ADB to extend the grant closing date from 31 December 2025 to 31 December 2026. The extension aims to provide sufficient time for MPW to complete the procurement processes on the recruitment of a consulting firm to prepare DED for the damaged sections of the Manatuto-Natarbora road utilizing the remaining grant funding. This exercise has been delayed due to the government's internal procurement processes.
Recruitment of a consulting firm for the preparation of DED for the Manatuto-Natarbora damaged sections: ADB through fax dated 5 February 2024 provided comments on the draft terms of reference and cost estimate for the detailed engineering design consultant in response to MPW's letter dated 23 January 2024. NPC on 26 August 2024 sought ADB approval on the draft terms of reference and cost estimate for the consulting services recruitment. ADB provided comments on 2 September 2024. NPC submitted Submission 1 on 22 September 2025 and ADB provided comments on mid-October 2025 and expected to be resolved by 30 November 2025.
Data Source: Project monitoring reports
